evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig, cutaneous application (Buehler-type), induction phase with 100% (undiluted) AURA, challenge phase on D29 with 100% AURA, readings at 24 h and 48 h; negative control: sterile water; positive control: 1% 2,4-dinitrochlorobenzene; 20 animals in test group.
evidence.support_text: In the guinea pig skin sensitization test, the test item (AURA, unextracted Aurantiochytrium limacinum biomass powder) showed 0% sensitized animals at both 24 and 48 h (20 animals with score 0). evidence.experimental_conditions: guinea pig, no sensitization observed

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig, topical application of EAMRP formulation, observation at 24 h
evidence.support_text: The skin sensitizing potential of the formulation was compared against positive control group i.e., 0.1% w/v CDNB, where extreme and intense sensitization responses were observed. evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs; technique that maximizes skin sensitization

evidence.experimental_conditions: in guinea pigs; references [12,22]

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test with 0.001%, 0.01%, 0.1%, 1.0%, and 5.0% aqueous Nonoxynol-6; weak nonvesicular reaction (+) at lower concentrations (0.001-0.1%), strong edematous or vesicular reaction (++) at higher concentrations (1.0% and 5.0%).
evidence.support_text: A 64-year-old metal industry worker who regularly immersed objects in fluid containing Nonoxynol-6 developed dermatitis on hands and forearms. Patch test results showed weak nonvesicular reactions (score +) to 0.001%, 0.01%, and 0.1% aqueous Nonoxynol-6 and strong edematous or vesicular reactions (score ++) to 1.0% and 5.0% Nonoxynol-6. No reactions were observed in a control group of 165 patients patch tested with 1.0% Nonoxynol-6.
